bundle.text:
# @wilshi/dsh-feishu bundle patch: the Feishu (Lark) surface over the
# dsh-base layer. Applied after dsh-base's insert; rows here override base
# rows by id, with the profile's own cordis.patch.yml and any --patch
# overlays still to come.
#
# This file inserts exactly ONE row: the surface itself. It starts in
# "not configured" mode until credentials are supplied (via the
# appId/appSecret config keys or the FEISHU_APP_ID / FEISHU_APP_SECRET
# environment variables), so the bundle is safe to add to any profile
# without credentials.
#
# Do NOT re-insert rows the host bundles already mount. `insert` does not
# dedupe (dsh-app-boot applyEntryPatches simply appends), so a duplicate
# service provider such as `@deepseek-ai/dsh-schedule` would mount twice
# (double store + double timers) and a duplicate `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user`
# row collides with the one the agent presets mount (dsh-tools rejects a
# duplicate tool name). Both are already provided:
#   - `schedule`        -> dsh-web-app/cordis.patch.yml
#   - `tool-ask-user`   -> dsh-web-app/presets/{standard,cordis,ptc}.patch.yml
# If this bundle ever needs custom schedule config, use an id-targeted
# override instead of an insert:
#   - id: schedule
#     config: { ... }
- insert:
    - id: feishu
      name: '@wilshi/dsh-feishu'
      config:
        locale: zh-CN
        sessionVisibility: chat

The Feishu UI for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) — a dsh-native plugin with a **panel-driven control console**: every slash command is a button on the ⚙️ control-panel card, approvals and questions resolve inside the chat, and one QR scan sets the whole app up.

readme.section: The Feishu UI for DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
readme.text:
> **Note:** [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) is
> still pre-release and may break between releases. This package is the
> **DSH `0.2.1-rc.5` port** of [PGZXB/dsh-feishu](https://github.com/PGZXB/dsh-feishu)
> (MIT): the upstream implementation is kept as-is in `lib/` and patched where
> the 0.2.1 host API changed. Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`, `cordis`) are
> `peerDependencies` — the DSH runtime supplies them.

The bundle patch inserts **only the `feishu` row**. It deliberately does not
re-insert `schedule` or `tool-ask-user`: DSH 0.2.1 already mounts them
(`dsh-web-app` and the agent presets), and `dsh-app-boot` appends `insert`
entries without dedupe — a duplicate service provider or tool name would fail
the boot. To customize schedule config, use an id-targeted override (see the
comments in `cordis.patch.yml`).

The plugin declares a minimal `inject` list — `agents`, `sessionQuery`,
`commands`, `tools` — so cordis waits for the services the chat surface cannot
work without. Everything else is an optional capability read through
`ctx.get(...)` and degraded with a warning: `approval`, `userQuestions`,
`attachments`, `workspaceRegistry`, `sessionTitle`, `permissionPresets`,
`planMode`, `agentDefaultModel`, `agentPresets`, `llm`, `schedule`,
`credentials`.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9163793-52f2-4e2c-a08a-22b27372be61

*2.5-min demo: control panel, streaming card, approval and question.*
```sh
node --version
npm install -g pnpm
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile feishu add @wilshi/dsh-feishu@latest

readme.section: 4. one QR scan — create + configure the Feishu app
readme.text: npx --yes --package @wilshi/dsh-feishu dsh-feishu-setup --new --profile feishu

npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile feishu
```
```sh
node --version
npm install -g pnpm

git clone https://github.com/WilShi/dsh-feishu.git
cd dsh-feishu
pnpm install
pnpm run build
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile feishu add link:.

readme.section: 5. one QR scan — create + configure the Feishu app
readme.text: pnpm run setup:feishu -- --new --profile feishu

npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile feishu
```

Then message the bot in Feishu. The setup wizard handles the Feishu app end
to end — no web-console work and no manual credentials. Already have an app?
Set `FEISHU_APP_ID` / `FEISHU_APP_SECRET` (environment or profile config)
instead — see [docs/feishu-setup.md](docs/feishu-setup.md).
```sh

readme.section: remove the plugin from the profile
readme.text: npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile feishu remove @wilshi/dsh-feishu

readme.section: (paths shown for the default dsh home, ~/.dsh)
readme.text:
rm -rf ~/.dsh/profiles/feishu ~/.dsh/feishu
```

A Feishu chat is a dsh session — the bot is the agent's avatar. A typical session goes like this: 1. **Start a chat.** Direct-message the bot, or run `/group ` to create a group the bot joins. In a group, @-mention the bot (the default policy; a group with just you and the bot also answers plain messages, and the policy is configurable).

2. **Open the control panel.** Send `panel` or `/panel` to open the card-based console.

3. **Pick a working directory.** Before the first turn, the bot opens the workspace picker automatically. The panel also offers **🗂️ Workspaces** with recent, favorite, searchable, and custom-path choices.

4. **Ask.** Send a message — the agent runs and its output streams into a live card (tool calls, reasoning, markdown, tables). The card ends green with the full answer inside; Stop, copy, retry, and the ⚙️ panel button sit on it. | Mid-stream | Finalized | |---|---| | | |

5. **Approve or answer when asked.** A permission escalation posts an
   approval card — tap **Allow once** (or **Reject**). A question posts a
   card you answer with a tap (or a reply).

| Approval | Question |
   |---|---|
   |  |  |

6. **Manage workspaces, sessions, and Agent modes.** **🗂️ Workspaces** lists the same
   registered names as DSH Desktop and can switch, add, search, favorite,
   rename, or safely remove a registration without deleting files or history.
    **🗂️ Sessions** filters by all sessions, current workspace, or this Feishu
    chat, then lets you inspect, resume, rename, fork, archive, or export.
    **🧠 Agent mode** switches between standard, Codex, Claude Code, and custom
    presets by preserving the current session and opening a safe new one.
   **➕ New chat** starts fresh without deleting the old session.
Every button on the panel card maps to a slash command — pick whichever feels faster; `/help` lists them all.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/help` | list all commands |
| `/panel` | open the control-panel card (all commands as buttons) |
| `/group <name>` | create a group with the bot (bare opens a name-input card) |
| `/cancel` | stop the running turn |
| `/cd <path>` | set this chat's working directory (bare opens a path-input card) |
| `/repo [path]` | pick a project directory (bare scans the default roots; `/repo <path>` scans that path) |
| `/workspaces [path]` | list and manage registered DSH workspaces; a path adds and switches directly |
| `/status` | show this chat's workspace, session, model, Agent mode, and run status |
| `/feishu-status` | show the surface diagnostic card |
| `/schedule` | list active reminders |
| `/model <provider/model>` | switch this session's model (bare opens the picker) |
| `/mode [preset]` | choose an Agent mode (standard, Codex, Claude Code, or a custom preset) |
| `/export` | send this chat's session log as a file |
| `/log` | send the Feishu-only diagnostic log to this chat; disabled unless an allowlist is configured or `allowLogExport: true` is explicitly set |
| `/sessions` | list saved sessions (resume, rename, fork, archive, or export f

- **Live streaming cards** — tool calls, reasoning, markdown, and tables stream in as the agent works.
- **One-tap control panel** — `/panel` renders the full command palette as buttons; no command syntax to remember, and each button is the exact equivalent of typing the command.
- **Card-based workspaces and sessions** — add, switch, search, favorite, rename, and safely remove registered workspaces; filter, resume, rename, fork, archive, and export sessions by all/workspace/chat scope.
- **Agent mode management** — choose standard, Codex, Claude Code, or a custom preset without mixing incompatible tool histories into the old session.
- **Native image and file input** — images enter DSH's native vision attachment path; files retain both a durable DSH reference and a workspace-readable path, with safe fallback when attachment storage is unavailable.
- **In-card approvals & questions** — approve a permission escalation or answer the agent's questions in the chat.
- **Sessions survive restarts** — a chat's session (and its working directory) is persisted across daemon restarts.
- **Groups & mentions** — @-mention the bot; error notices, approvals, and questions @ the requester.

- `interactionTimeoutMs` controls how long approval and question cards wait for a reply (default: 5 minutes; minimum: 1000 ms).
- `locale` defaults to `zh-CN` and may be set to `en-US`; `sessionVisibility` defaults to `chat`. Administrators may explicitly widen it to `workspace` or `all` on a trusted private bot.
- Session visibility applies to lists, direct `/resume <id>`, and every session card action. An active session cannot be silently moved from one Feishu chat to another.
- `maxQueuedTurns` limits messages waiting behind a running turn (default: 50); `maxPendingAttachments` limits files waiting for the next instruction (default: 20). Excess work is refused with a visible notice instead of growing durable state without bounds.
- The session map automatically reads legacy v1/v2 data and upgrades it to v3 without replacing credentials, chat bindings, or working directories.
- Persistent logs contain only records from the `feishu` logger, rotate at 5 MiB, and retain 3 archives by default. Override these limits with `logMaxBytes` and `logMaxFiles`.

Join the dsh-feishu community group on Feishu:

- **[PGZXB/dsh-feishu](https://github.com/PGZXB/dsh-feishu)** — the original
  dsh-feishu implementation this package ports to DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 (MIT). All
  Host/Client logic and the setup wizard come from upstream; this repository
  keeps the compiled `lib/` and patches only the host API seams.
- **[botmux](https://github.com/deepcoldy/botmux)** — the reference for the
  group-chat interaction patterns: streaming cards, approvals, and the
  QR-driven Open Platform quick-setup flow. dsh-feishu borrows botmux's
  *interaction and onboarding patterns*, not its architecture — botmux
  bridges external CLIs, while this surface is dsh-native and in-process.
- **[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)** —
  the platform this surface is built for.
- **[Lark Open Platform SDK](https://github.com/larksuite/node-sdk)** — the
  WebSocket long connection and card APIs the transport builds on.
